analysis:
Examined both added test files, the mock close-helper patch, all supplied surrounding BASE source and file metadata against the canonical definition index and selected details. No concrete security regression is supported in this test-only scope. CoordinatorReconnectPolicyTests.swift:32-93 checks the 60-second reset boundary, jitter ranges, repeated 1012 closes without backoff growth, and preserved exponential delays for transport failures and other codes. NetworkFrameworkCloseCodeTests.swift:19-68 checks named codes, unknown-code payload parsing, nonzero-index slices, short payloads and actual mock close-frame delivery. Its plaintext TCP connection is to the existing loopback test server (MockCoordinator.swift BASE:279-315), not evidence of weakened production transport. MockCoordinator.swift HEAD:447-456 parameterizes test close codes/reasons while preserving the default 1001 close and lock-protected removal of the outbound writer. Existing mock attestation, encryption, message capture and routing behavior is unchanged; no new prompt/key disclosure, billing, cache, privileged-helper or qualification behavior is shown.
Integration must verify the production policy/parser and CoordinatorClient receive/run-loop changes, which are not supplied here: close-code capture must survive transport callback ordering, fast 1012 reconnects must remain cancellation-aware, and connection replacement must invalidate serving authorization and stale queued work (TB-002, TB-011, T-053, A-016; cancellation relates to T-010). These tests establish expected ranges and framework behavior, not those production lifecycle guarantees. Missing production source is a coverage limit rather than an observed missing control.
